what_changed.text: DXY broke below 100 for the first time since mid-2024. Dollar weakness score escalated 0 → 1.
Commodity/Gold ratio collapsed 39% YoY — now scoring at maximum. This is a monetary signal, not inflation.
Gold momentum and Gold/Treasury Divergence both remain at maximum intensity. No signs of weakening.

contrarian: Wall Street is framing gold’s run as an inflation trade. The framework says otherwise. If this were inflation, commodities would be running with gold — copper, oil, and the GSCI would be surging. Instead, the commodity/gold ratio has collapsed 39%. Gold is repricing against everything: stocks, bonds, and commodities alike.

This is a monetary confidence signal. Gold is telling you something about the monetary system itself, not about CPI prints. The last time gold posted 40%+ YoY gains while Treasury yields stayed flat was the early 1970s — after Nixon closed the gold window but before the market fully processed the implications.

Meanwhile, the Fed is quietly expanding its balance sheet through $40B/month in short-duration purchases while publicly maintaining a tightening stance. The framework sees through the narrative to the mechanism: the balance sheet is growing, and the purchases are only “short duration” for now.

divergence.description: The single most predictive indicator in the framework. When gold surges and yields don’t follow, the bond market is being artificially suppressed — either through direct purchases or implicit policy. This divergence preceded every major regime transition in the last 50 years.
divergence.current_reading: Current reading: Gold +41% YoY while 10Y yields are flat (−0.03%). The gold-colored area shows the divergence widening — gold is screaming while the bond market stays quiet. Historically, this gap closes violently: either yields spike to catch up (bad for bonds), or gold is proven right about debasement (bad for the monetary system).

positioning.intro: Elevated is the building phase, not the panic phase. Historically, the transition from Elevated to Crisis takes 6–18 months, and the largest gains in gold, Bitcoin, and hard assets occur during the transition — not after crisis is confirmed. The investors who outperformed in 2009–2011 and 1972–1974 were positioned before the transition, not after.

posture.label: Gold — overweight, core
posture.reason: Gold Momentum + Divergence both at 2 simultaneously. Historically, 12-month forward returns from this signal cluster averaged 35–60%.

posture.label: Bitcoin — overweight, debasement call option
posture.reason: Functions as high-beta gold in monetary regime transitions. Dropped 57% in 2020 acute crisis, then 18x’d. Position size for volatility.

posture.label: Critical materials — hold exposure
posture.reason: Copper physical premium at 4% — below the 5% trigger but elevated. If China escalates export controls (score moves 0→1+), this becomes an overweight.

posture.label: Duration — begin reducing
posture.reason: The Gold/Treasury Divergence says yields are artificially suppressed. When the divergence closes, long bonds are the most exposed asset class.

posture.label: Long Treasuries — underweight
posture.reason: If the framework is right about stealth suppression, long-duration bonds carry asymmetric downside. Reduce before the divergence forces a repricing.

posture.label: Equities — selective only
posture.reason: Favor companies with monopoly pricing power and real asset backing. Avoid rate-sensitive growth. S&P/Gold ratio at 2.03 and falling — equities losing purchasing power.

escalation: Fed shifts to long-duration purchases → immediate Transition (Override Rule #4). This is the bright red line.
Treasury auction B/C drops below 2.0 → demand crisis signal. Currently masked by Fed purchases — watch what happens if they pause.
Gold breaks +60% YoY with 8-week acceleration >15% → Gold Momentum maxes. Currently +41% — still room.
deescalation: Gold YoY drops below +30% while yields rise → genuine tightening. Divergence closes from the gold side.
Fed resumes QT at full pace → balance sheet contracting. Not just slowing purchases — actively shrinking.
Deficit/GDP falls below 5% → structural fiscal pressure easing. Currently at 5.9% and rising.
